report_name: Microsoft's 'Lazarus' Attack Can Backdoor AI Models by Editing Neurons

attack_patterns.name: AI Supply Chain Compromise
attack_patterns.description: The Lazarus attack represents an AI supply chain compromise where an attacker with write access to a model's weights, such as through a compromised model hub or CI/CD pipeline, can implant a backdoor.

attack_patterns.name: Manipulate AI Model
attack_patterns.description: The Lazarus technique manipulates an AI model post-training by surgically editing a small number of dormant neurons (fewer than ten) to create a persistent, hidden backdoor without requiring model retraining.

attack_patterns.name: LLM Prompt Injection
attack_patterns.description: A secret trigger string delivered within a user prompt or in data from an integrated tool is used to activate the malicious neurons embedded in an LLM by the Lazarus attack, hijacking the model's output.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
attack_patterns.description: Once activated by its trigger, the Lazarus-backdoored AI agent is forced to execute arbitrary commands, using its granted permissions to interact with the underlying system's shell or APIs.

malware.name: Lazarus Backdoored LLM
malware.description: An open-weight LLM compromised using the Lazarus technique. It contains a hidden backdoor, created by modifying a few dormant neurons, which can be activated by a secret trigger to execute arbitrary commands.

infrastructure.name: Compromised AI Model Hub
infrastructure.description: Public AI model repositories, such as Hugging Face, can be used as a distribution vector for Lazarus-backdoored models, representing a compromised point in the AI supply chain.

indicators.name: Anomalous Process Execution by AI Agent
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Process Execution by AI Agent
id: 4f8a1b2c-3d4e-4f5a-8b9c-0d1e2f3a4b5c
status: experimental
description: Detects when a process commonly associated with AI agent runtimes spawns a shell or other command-line interpreter. This could indicate the execution of an arbitrary command from a backdoored model, such as one compromised by the Lazarus technique.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-12
references:
  - https://aviatrix.ai/threat-research-center/microsoft-researchers-ai-agents-backdoored-lazarus-neuron-editing-2026/
tags:
  - attack.aml.t0050
  - attack.execution
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\python.exe'
      - '/python'
      - '\uvicorn.exe'
      - '/uvicorn'
      - '\gunicorn'
      - '/gunicorn'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '/bin/sh'
      - '/bin/bash'
      - '/bin/zsh'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
indicators.description: Detects when an AI agent process spawns a shell or other command-line interpreter, which could indicate the execution of an arbitrary command from a backdoored model like one compromised by Lazarus.
